channel.title: mindoff.work
channel.description: Open-source tools, research notes, and product experiments for designing quieter, lighter, more useful ways to work.

item.title: AI Has No Soul
item.description: AI can write the code, generate the art, and pass the demo. What it cannot do is leave something of itself in the work. That gap shows up in the parts of a product users actually feel.

item.title: In Defense of Every AI Opinion
item.description: Every position on AI in software development has valid ground. The thing that separates good outcomes from bad ones isn't the position itself. It's whether your product can handle that position's assumptions.

item.title: How I Turned Data Pipeline Headaches Into a Python Library
item.description: After building two financial calculation engines and solving the same infrastructure problems from scratch each time, the patterns were consistent enough to turn into a reusable library. This is what that observation looked like.

item.title: Mindoff Dataport
item.description: A Python Package to extract xlsx templates with full visual fidelity and render data-driven reports in xlsx and PDF formats.

item.title: How I Keep AI in Its Place
item.description: Not every part of a software build should be handed to AI. Here is the framework I use to decide which parts should, and why getting that line wrong is harder to notice than it sounds.

item.title: Django Mindoff
item.description: Architectural framework to build production-ready Django REST APIs faster with less boilerplate.

item.title: Writing Python Docstrings for MkDocs
item.description: A compact, Markdown-first docstring style for Python projects that auto-generate API reference pages with MkDocs, keeping exact API facts close to code without duplicating them in guide pages.

item.title: Versioned MkDocs Docs with Mike, GitHub Pages, and a Custom Domain
item.description: A practical, opinionated walkthrough of the documentation strategy I use across my Python projects: versioned MkDocs output on a dedicated branch, Mike for release aliases, and GitHub Pages serving a custom domain.

item.title: 4 Rules to Keep a Prototype Honest
item.description: A useful prototype answers one risky question clearly. Polish applied before that question is answered makes an idea comfortable to approve while leaving its hardest problem untouched.

item.title: Mindoff Weblog
item.description: A personal publishing site rebuilt around static files, MDX, and GitHub Pages — designed to stay available and low-maintenance without a server or a database.

item.title: Solving Memory Pressure in a Python Data Pipeline
item.description: After a vectorized rewrite cut processing time from 30 minutes to 10 seconds, concurrent load under limited server memory exposed a completely different constraint, and the solution required batching, job queues, and polling to solve without giving back the performance gains.

item.title: 4 Types of Test Cases Every Python Developer Should Write
item.description: Most developers write valid-path tests and stop, unsure if they've covered enough. This four-category model gives you a repeatable system for test coverage you can actually reason about.

item.title: Git Cherry-Pick. When to Use It and When to Walk Away
item.description: Git cherry-pick lets you move individual commits between branches surgically. Here's when that precision saves you and when it quietly turns into a merge problem later.

item.title: How I Replaced For Loops with Vectorized Pandas
item.description: A hands-on account of replacing loop-based data processing with vectorized pandas operations across two financial calculation engines, and what that architectural shift actually looks like in code.

item.title: Git Cheat Sheet for Everyday Development
item.description: The Git commands that actually come up in real development work, explained for people in a hurry. Covers everyday workflow, merge conflicts, pull vs fetch vs rebase, undoing commits, branch cleanup, and the gitignore cache fix you'll need sooner or later.

item.title: 5 Pandas Operations That Replace Most For Loops
item.description: A practical walkthrough of the merge, reduce, pivot, and column math operations that together replace almost every for loop in a production data processing pipeline, with worked examples and the reasoning behind each.

item.title: Convert Markdown to Structured JSON for Cleaner React Rendering
item.description: A Python pipeline that converts Markdown files into structured JSON, handling GitHub Gist embeds as first-class elements so React components can render text, images, and code separately.

item.title: A Minimalist's Guide to Engineered Wood
item.description: Eight engineered wood types distilled into intentional choices. A guide for builders who want to pick the right material once, avoid the common mistakes, and get on with the work.
